correctness.rationale: The exact homogeneous-polynomial boundary reduction produces forward/reverse signed Kac sums. Gaussian sphere homogeneity allows independent N(0,1) coefficients. Their q_m norm divided by sqrt(m) converges in probability to 1 because q_m=2m/(m+1) and sample moments converge with uniformly controlled variance. The jointly interpolated same/alternating-sign partial sums converge to two independent Brownian motions: same-sign covariance tends to min(u,v), cross-sign covariance is bounded by 1/m, and Gaussian fourth-moment tightness controls the functional limit. Exact Abel summation and the positive-weight Lipschitz map Phi_s establish uniform convergence for all s>=0, including s=infinity, for each of four forward/reversed profiles, so the continuous mapping theorem gives the stated inverse Gaussian-process supremum. The supremum is positive finite almost surely, and Wiener full support provides all positive values. Independent implementation checked 56 signed Abel identities across m=2,5,17,71 and seven scales, maximum error 2.22e-16. The finite checks are corroboration only; the functional invariance and uniform boundary argument provide the proof.
